mussels.scope: Selected actual scientific summary read, not all 888 web lines or images. No unverified blanket ballast-law chronology/mandate or modelled economic-total estimate is imported.

facts: An invasive organism is introduced outside its natural/historical distribution and causes harm. Species native to one Canadian region may be invasive after introduction elsewhere.
DFO describes ecological harm and infrastructure/management costs; being foreign or dangerous alone does not establish invasive status.
Zebra and quagga mussels originated in the Caspian/Black Sea regions and reached North America through ships’ ballast water. Later spread can involve currents and boats moving between water bodies.
Both compete with native mussels for food/space and can attach to their shells, restricting feeding/movement. Filtering alters food webs; effects differ across organisms and water bodies.
These mussels can foul water intakes and other infrastructure. Their presence is not proof every ecological effect is negative for every species, or that all lakes respond identically.
limits: No precise first-introduction year, current legal-compliance rule, individual lake prediction or child field sampling is required.
Secondary drift of a population originally introduced by people is not the same historical pathway as an organism naturally extending its native range.
